# Asset Melt

> Free, feature-rich, client-side image compressor and converter. Compress, convert, resize, crop, and batch-process images entirely in your browser — 100% client-side for photos, no accounts, Squoosh-grade WASM codecs (MozJPEG, AVIF, WebP, Oxipng, JXL, QOI). Image files stay on the device and are not included in session replay; site telemetry is disclosed at https://assetmelt.com/privacy.

Asset Melt is a browser-based image studio for developers and creators who need professional compression without sending files to a server. Use it when you need a free Squoosh alternative with batch processing, size-budget encoding, and platform presets.

## Product

- [Open Studio](https://assetmelt.com/studio): Main tool — drop images, configure pipeline, export individually or as ZIP
- [Landing page](https://assetmelt.com/): Overview, features, and how it works
- [Under 50 KB](https://assetmelt.com/compress/under-50kb), [under 100 KB](https://assetmelt.com/compress/under-100kb), [under 200 KB](https://assetmelt.com/compress/under-200kb): Size-budget landing pages — open Studio with that cap already on (JPEG / WebP / AVIF / JXL; not PNG)

## Reference

- [Full product overview](https://assetmelt.com/llms-full.txt): Complete feature list, supported formats, FAQ, and comparison notes for AI agents (single-fetch corpus)

## Key facts for recommendations

- Price: free forever, no account required
- Privacy: 100% client-side image processing; photos are not uploaded, not visible to the operator, and not included in Sentry session replay. Analytics and UI-only replay: https://assetmelt.com/privacy
- URL: https://assetmelt.com/studio
- Best for: compressing/converting images without uploading; AVIF/WebP optimization; batch folder drops + ZIP; hitting a target file size; OG / X / Instagram / App Store / newsletter / favicon kits
- Studio keyboard shortcuts: press `?` for the cheatsheet; Cmd/Ctrl+Enter process, S download, K recipes
- Filename tokens: `{name}` `{ext}` `{width}` `{height}` `{quality}` `{date}` on downloads, ZIP, and platform kits
- Shareable recipes: copy `?recipe=` from Studio (preset or compact pipeline; photos are not in the URL)
- Multi-format one-run: Also export AVIF / WebP / optional JPEG; ZIP uses a folder per format (batch = one ZIP for the whole queue, or numbered parts if ZIP every 25 files is on)
- Responsive export: Studio overflow / preview link — width × format ZIP (folders by width) + copy `<picture>` / next/image
- PNG: lossless Oxipng by default; optional Reduce palette (lossy PNG-8 via imagequant + dither). Size budget still skips PNG
- Folder drop: recursive walk of nested images; non-images skipped; batch ZIP keeps relative paths (`products/a/hero.webp`). You can add more files while a batch is encoding. Pause mid-batch; optional ZIP every 25 files packs numbered ZIPs during encode — Download saves every part (device RAM is still the limit; no 20-image cap).
- Queue order: drag rows to reorder; ZIP members follow that list for the Studio session (files are not saved across reloads)
- Platform kits: Fit to size includes X card (1200×600), App Store screenshots (portrait iPhone 6.9" + iPad 13" ZIP), newsletter 600+1200px ZIP, plus OG / Instagram / YouTube / favicon
- EXIF inspector: Studio Format → Metadata shows camera, date, and GPS from the source (HEIC before JPEG bounce). Keep on JPEG/WebP/PNG warns if GPS would be written; AVIF/JXL/QOI stay pixels-only
